customer_question: What product materials do we need to provide for the Compliance Folder, can we submit materials for only one of our models, and what happens after we send them?
question_variants: If the Product List includes multiple models but we can only provide a detailed outline drawing for one model, is that acceptable?
How will the Compliance Folder be delivered, and how long must we keep it?
If we release future models with the same module/host stack, do we need a new registration?
actual_issue: After completing the registration's review-page confirmation, Allion requested the customer provide Compliance Folder materials: (1) the product's operation manual (the portion describing Bluetooth-related operation, draft-level acceptable), (2) the product's block diagram, and (3) the product's outline (external appearance) drawing. The customer replied that, of the models in the registration, only the 'NXA-S' model had a detailed outline drawing available, and asked if providing materials for that one model only was sufficient; Allion confirmed this was fine ('1モデルの資料で問題ありません'). After registration finalization, Allion compiled the Compliance Folder (CD-R) using these materials plus registration-process documents and shipped it to the customer via Japan Post Click Post with a tracking number, reiterating the 1-year post-discontinuation retention requirement, audit-only presentation (likened to a vehicle inspection certificate, with reassurance that no supported customer has been audited), and the free derivative-model registration path via 'Manage Submitted Products' on My Page for future models sharing the same module/host stack.
plain_english_explanation: For the Compliance Folder, the customer needs to supply three types of product materials: the Bluetooth-relevant portion of the operation manual (a draft is acceptable), a block diagram, and an outline/external-appearance drawing. If a registration's Product List covers multiple models but the customer can only provide a detailed outline drawing for one representative model, that single model's materials are sufficient for the Compliance Folder - a complete set of materials for every listed model isn't required. After registration is finalized, the consultant compiles all materials (including documents obtained during the registration process itself) onto a CD-R and ships it via trackable mail. As with other registrations, the customer must retain this Compliance Folder for one year after sales of the registered products end, present it only if SIG requests an audit, and can register future derivative models (same module/host stack) for free via Manage Submitted Products.

decision_logic: Request the standard three Compliance Folder materials (Bluetooth-relevant operation manual section, block diagram, outline drawing). If the registration covers multiple models but the customer can only provide complete materials (especially outline drawings) for one representative model, accept that as sufficient rather than requiring per-model documentation. After finalization, compile and ship the Compliance Folder via trackable mail with standard retention/audit and derivative-registration guidance.
final_recommendation: Accept Compliance Folder materials for a single representative model when a registration's Product List covers multiple models but complete materials (e.g., outline drawings) aren't available for all of them, and proceed with standard Compliance Folder compilation, delivery, retention/audit guidance, and derivative-model registration information.
risk_if_done_wrong: Requiring complete per-model documentation when only one model's materials are available could unnecessarily delay Compliance Folder creation and delivery, holding up closeout of the registration engagement.
